newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares move higher on selective trade.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares move higher on selective trade.

text.p: Istanbul stocks gained on selective buys prompted by first half profit expectations in companies, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 ended 31 points, or 1.55 percent higher at 2,034 after brushing a high of 2,044 in early trade. But daily trade volume shrank by 27 percent to 21.05 trillion lira from Tuesday's 28.89 trillion.
"The cash that was freed from the state shares has been flowing into shares with high first half profit expectations," said one broker.
He added that technically, the market's new index target was 2,150 points for this next week.
But other brokers said the lack of fresh liquidity inflow could hinder the market.
The most heavily traded stock of the day was largely state-owned flat steel producer Eregli, up 1,000 lira at 28,000. It made up 10.6 percent of the total volume.
Eregli was followed by largely state-owned petroleum products distributor Petrol Ofisi up 2,000 lira at 32,500 and Akbank, unchanged at 10,250 lira.

Of the 250 shares traded, gainers outdid losers sharply by 152 to 43 while 55 remained unchanged. The IMKB Industrial gained 1.92 percent to 1,967, the IMKB Services jumped 3.02 percent to 1,978 and the IMKB Financial ended 1.51 percent higher at 2,212.
